title: Ringed slice over an arbitrary sheaf: element-site presentation and exact extension by zero
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $A$ be a sheaf of sets in the chosen universe. Form the site $\mathcal C/A$ whose objects are pairs $(U,s)$ with $U\in\mathcal C$ and $s\in A(U)$, whose arrows $(V,t)\to(U,s)$ are arrows $v:V\to U$ with $A(v)(s)=t$, and whose covering families are those whose underlying families in $\mathcal C$ cover. This is a small site. There is a geometric equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/A)\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/A$ taking $(F\xrightarrow p A)$ to $((U,s)\mapsto\{x\in F(U):p(x)=s\})$. Under this equivalence the ring $R_A=R\times A\to A$ corresponds to the sheaf $(U,s)\mapsto R(U)$. The localization geometric morphism $j_A:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/A\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ has module pullback $j_A^*:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_A)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] given by $(j_A^*M)(U,s)=M(U)$. This functor is exact and has an exact additive left adjoint $j_{A!}$. For an $R_A$-module sheaf $L$ on $\mathcal C/A$, $j_{A!}L$ is the module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the presheaf $U\mapsto\bigoplus_{s\in A(U)}L(U,s)$; restriction along $v:V\to U$ sends the summand indexed by $s$ to that indexed by $A(v)(s)$ using the restriction of $L$. For any map of sheaves $B\to A$, applying this construction inside $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/A$ identifies its localization at $B\to A$ with $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/B$, with restricted ring $R_B$; the resulting restriction composed with $j_A^*$ is canonically $j_B^*$.

proof.text: Apply element-site descent to obtain the topology equality, fibre equivalence with its natural fibre identification, cocontinuity of the projection and continuity of each map of element sites.

Apply the continuous-cocontinuous ringed restriction theorem to the element projection and R. Its identity structural map and module adjunction supply localization, its inverse-image formula, the identity ring-map formula, and the right adjoint to module restriction.

Choose the canonical Mathlib module extension of the element projection. Its adjunction to restriction is already proved in the construction module. The section formula for restriction and the ring formula are definitional equalities.

Use the presheaf extension computation and Mathlib SheafOfModules.pullbackIso. Applying module sheafification to the resulting presheaf isomorphism identifies canonical extension with sheafification of the displayed direct-sum presheaf.

The extension preserves finite limits because its pullbackIso expresses it as forget-to-presheaves, the left-exact presheaf extension, and exact module sheafification. It preserves finite colimits as a left adjoint. Restriction preserves finite limits as the right adjoint in the extension adjunction and finite colimits as the left adjoint to localization.modules. The extension is additive because a finite-colimit-preserving functor preserves binary biproducts and zero morphisms.

For B→A use descent for B and the proved continuity of its element map. Choose the defined elementModulePullbackOver. The composite restriction is naturally isomorphic to elementModulePullback R B by Iso.refl: its objects, restrictions, scalar actions and morphism maps reduce to the identical original module operations.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NA-7a3797386 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, all six steps, every cited statement, and Stacks sites.tex 0791 and sites-modules.tex 04IE (1)-(4), 04J4 and 03DJ. The statement matches the sources and is not weakened. Step 1 (the element site) is correct. In step 2 (the fibre equivalence) the presheaf of pairs is already a sheaf, so the extra sheafification is harmless. Step 6 (relocalization) is correct: s is determined by b, the coverings agree and the ring maps are identities. The three clause-restating helper nodes are gone, so the D1 return is repaired. I fixed three faults in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-proper-base-change/lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction.json. F1 (step 4): the u_p comma category had its arrows reversed, and A(f)(t) with f:V->U and t in A(V) is ill-typed. It now uses the triples (V,t,phi:U->V); the discrete part {(U,s,id)} is final, which gives the direct sum over s in A(U). F2 (step 5, E3): exactness of j_{A!} applied a direct sum to a short exact sequence of sheaves as if it were exact on each section, which is false because sheaf epimorphisms are only locally surjective. It now uses the 03DJ argument: right exact as a left adjoint, plus injectivity from injective maps on sections, exact sheafification (lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact) and the faithful forgetful functor that preserves kernels (lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful). F3 (steps 3 and 5): j_A existing as a morphism of topoi and j_A^* preserving cokernels had no support, and the step treated a definition as if it supplied the morphism. The repair shows that p is continuous and cocontinuous and cites lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction and lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction (structure map id, R_A tensor over R_A of M is M). So j_A^* is a left adjoint, and it is exact because kernels are computed on sections. Both added nodes are reviewed and in unit sk-thm-properbasechange. A DFS found no cycle through the item or its citer lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport. The module-colimits lemma is in sk-thm-reduction, which the unit cites, so it stays on the route and no tool_uses are needed. The duplicate search found only the representable-object versions, and the edge cases (A terminal, A initial, two sections, B=A) are consistent. Statement, stmt_deps, blueprint and searches are unchanged; no nodes added or dropped.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer

    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}) (A : Sheaf J (Type u)) :
    Nonempty (RingedSheafSliceAdjunctionData R A)
lean.note: Section 1(B): the published RingedSheafSliceAdjunctionData had localization.modules ⊣ pullback. The direct image j_A* is right adjoint to restriction j_A^*, so that field had the opposite direction and asserted a false adjunction for an infinite sheaf over the point. This module retains the existing element-site construction, fibre equivalence, canonical rings, module restriction and extension-by-zero data, and changes only that field to pullback ⊣ localization.modules, with its proof explanation. It now states the dependency node as written: j_A! ⊣ j_A^* ⊣ j_A*. No natural-language node field is changed. U3: existing construction declarations are moved verbatim to Sheaf.CategoryTheory.RingedSheafSliceConstruction and publicly re-exported; their types and names are unchanged. The existence theorem is proved from three fully proved supporting constructions using canonical Mathlib adjoints; no sorry remains in the delivery.
